Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

SampleSizeCalc 3.1.2

  • calculate() now enforces study design and parameter invariants:
    • singleMean precision planning searches for the smallest integer \(N \ge 2\) satisfying the Student \(t\) CI half-width constraint, resolving oscillation between adjacent rounded fixed-point iterates and preventing \(N = 1\) returns.
    • diagAccuracy dual-endpoint planning (dual = TRUE) evaluates diseased-case and non-diseased-control quotas separately. Expected screening totals convert the two rounded strata quotas by prevalence and 1 - prevalence respectively.
    • cohort person-time planning preserves the original rate0 and rate1 labels and allocation when rate1 < rate0 (protective exposure), maintaining the user’s intended design.
    • paired designs default to pairing = "within_subject" (counting one person per pair, two measurements); specify pairing = "matched_subjects" for pairs of distinct people.
    • bioequivalence integrates exact conditional TOST power over the variance distribution and aborts if target power cannot be reached within 10,000 subjects.
    • diagLR validates target direction (upper limit > expected for LR-; lower limit < expected for LR+).
    • Kappa planning validates that inputs define a valid joint probability table.
    • Result objects now validate count positivity, integer values, and that group counts sum to reported totals. Power-curve replay retains user-specified alpha.
  • calculate() and sample_size_calculator() now reject unsupported, misspelled, duplicate, unnamed, and inactive-branch design arguments. In particular, dropout outside cohort proportion planning and alternative outside the supported diagnostic test raise an error.
  • diagAUC and diagAUCCompare testing now consistently use ratio as controls per case, independently of var_method (default "binormal"). Supply either a fixed ratio or clinical prevalence, not both. Cases and controls are rounded before summing total_subjects; total_subjects_to_screen is returned only for clinical recruitment and meets both quotas in expectation. AUC calculation reports use the same variance model, test convention, and rounding as the calculation.
  • predictiveModel binary planning now takes the maximum of Riley B1, B3, and B4, including the Nagelkerke R-squared optimism criterion. For prevalence 0.05, 10 parameters, Cox-Snell R-squared 0.2, and shrinkage 0.9, the corrected size is 542 rather than 398, matching pmsampsize. B2 MAPE remains informational, and its inputs are validated.
  • twoOrdinal now sums the separately rounded group sizes, including unequal allocation. The normalized Machin example needs 31 per arm, 62 total; Whitehead’s example needs 94 per arm, 188 total.
  • Numeric design inputs now require finite scalars (with category proportions as the documented vector exception). Missing and infinite values produce argument-specific errors, including in screen_required() and mrmc_power().
  • Zero-effect planning inputs (mean1 == mean2, p1 == p2, meanDiff == 0, and equal expected proportions in an unpaired diagnostic comparison) now abort with argument-specific errors instead of leaking base-R root-finding failures.
  • sample_size_calculator() now rejects ... names that R’s partial matching would silently bind to design, alpha, or power: a misspelled p used to set power without warning, and d clobbered design when the design keyword was passed positionally. Exact control names keep working, including named design calls that pass a design-specific d.

SampleSizeCalc 3.1.1

  • The package is named SampleSizeCalc; use library(SampleSizeCalc) and SampleSizeCalc::calculate() in new scripts.

Corrections (P0 series: wrong formulas / wrong citations)

  • steppedWedge had sigma^2 and tau^2 swapped in Hussey & Hughes Eq 8. The printed equation (p. 187) is Var = I*sigma^2*(sigma^2 + T*tau^2) / [(IU-W)*sigma^2 + (U^2+ITU-TW-IV)*tau^2], where sigma^2 is the cluster-mean variance (sigma2_ind/m) and tau^2 the between-cluster variance. The previous code had the two factors interchanged. For the paper’s own Washington EPT example (I=24, T=5, m=100, p=0.05, CV=0.3) it returned SE=0.00486 and power=0.959 at RR=0.64, whereas Eq 8 gives SE=0.006638 and power=0.774, consistent with the paper’s “about 80% power to detect a decrease in prevalence of roughly 36%”. The spurious “80% crossing at RR=0.73” claim is withdrawn.
  • twoOrdinal was missing the allocation factor (1+phi)^2/phi. Machin et al. (2018) Eq 4.3 (p. 57) is N = Gamma (1+phi)^2/phi (z_{1-a/2}+z_{1-b})^2/(log OR)^2 with Gamma = 3/(1-sum pbar^3) (Eq 4.4); Whitehead (1993) Eq 10 (p. 2260) is n = 3(A+1)^2 (u_{a/2}+u_b)^2 / [A theta^2 (1-sum pbar^3)]. They are algebraically identical with A = phi, and at phi = 1 the factor is 4. The previous code omitted it and returned one quarter of the required size (e.g. 16 instead of 61 for Machin Example 4.1). New allocation argument (default 1) exposes unequal allocation. Verified against Machin Example 4.1 (N4 = 60.09 -> 60) and Whitehead Example 1 (n = 187, 94 per group).
  • kappa_Q() now implements Cantor (1996) Eq 3 verbatim. The previous p_o(1-p_o)/(1-p_e)^2 coincides with Cantor’s Q only when both marginal rating proportions are 0.5. Cantor’s expression is `Q = (1-pi_e)^(-4) * { sum_i pi_ii[(1-pi_e) - (pi_i. + pi_.i)(1-pi_o)]^2
    • (1-pi_o)^2 * sum_{i!=j} pi_ij(pi_.i + pi_j.)^2 - (pi_o pi_e - 2pi_e + pi_o)^2 }with the Eq 4 identities. The implementation now reproduces **Cantor Table 1** at all 18 spot-checked cells and **Table 2** at all 5 maxima ((0.3,0.3) 1.07003 at kappa=0.187,(0.4,0.4) 1.00558 at 0.067,(0.5,0.5) 1.00000 at 0,(0.7,0.3) 0.52438 at 0,(0.9,0.1) 0.04819 at 0`), plus both worked examples (165 and 214). The earlier claim that “pi = 0.3 gives Q = 1.0” was arithmetically impossible.
  • AUC variance default is now binormal (Zhou Eq 6.5). The exponential form (Eq 6.4) systematically under-estimates variance for ordinal results (Zhou p. 197), and the binormal form is what Zhou’s own CTC example (p. 198, n = 46) and Hajian-Tilaki’s Table 7 use. var_method remains selectable. This makes diagAUC reproduce the book’s n = 13 CTC superiority anchor (the previous one-sided Z_alpha convention gave 10) and diagAUCCompare reproduce Hajian’s n = 211 example (was 185).
  • singleMean now iterates the Student t quantile (Machin 2018 Eq 9.18, p. 152), instead of using the normal z once. Machin explicitly requires the iteration when N0 < 40. sigma=3, d=0.5 now gives 141 (was 139; Bhardwaj’s z-only arithmetic prints 138.29 -> 138). The hints field reports the starting value when it is below 40.
  • cohort + rate swaps the two rates when rate1 < rate0 and says so in hints, so the exposed/unexposed person-time columns stay meaningful. ratio is now documented consistently as the exposed:unexposed person-time ratio (Machin Eq 6.2, p. 84).
  • singleArmPhaseII minimax now matches Simon/clinfun exactly. The tie-break is “minimise N, then minimise EN(p0)”, reproducing Machin 2018 Example 17.2 (1/15, 5/25) and clinfun::ph2simon for both (0.1, 0.3) and (0.2, 0.4).
  • clusterRCT upgraded to Machin (2018) Eq 12.10 (Student t correction). The previous implementation wrapped the individually-randomised answer in DE = 1+(m-1)ICC and rounded twice (once on subjects, once on clusters), which over-stated the cluster count. The new implementation follows Eq 12.10 (p. 199): `N = DE * [ (1+phi)^2/phi * (z_{1-a/2}+z_{1-b})2/(delta/sigma)2
    • z^2_{1-a/2}/2 ], rounds **once at the cluster level**, and reproduces **Machin Example 12.1 (p. 206) exactly**: delta=3.5, sigma=6.94, m=2, ICC=0.025, 2-sided alpha=0.05, power=0.90 -> **N=172, K=86, 43 per arm** (was 176/44). The ICC sensitivity in the same example is also reproduced (rho=0.1 -> 184, rho=0.2 -> 204). Newcluster_size_inflation()exposes Eq 12.5 (constant m) and Eq 12.7 (variable m viacv_m), and Eq 12.12/12.13 give the binarysigma_Planandrho_Binary`.
  • crossover reported a double-counted total. Julious (2004) Eq 6.6 (Section 6.3 “Cross-over trials”) writes n as the total sample size, so n_required is now the per-sequence count and total_n = 2 * n_required. The previous code used the total as n_required and then doubled it again. Example: delta=2, sigma_w=3 now gives 18 per sequence / 36 total (was 36/72). Senn (2002) Section 9.5.1 (Eq 9.18-9.20, pp. 278-280) confirms the parameterisation (sigma^2 = 2 sigma_w^2, Var = sigma^2/n, df = n-2, n = total with n/2 per sequence) and refines it with a Student t correction; the hints field now says so.
  • mrmc_power() now implements Zhou Eq 6.32 verbatim. The previous code used (1 - rho1) instead of (1 - rho_b), divided the patient-sampling variance sigma_c2 by n, and added a spurious rho2*sigma_b2*((1-rho1)+(J-1)(rho2-rho3)) term. With the book’s own mammography parameters it returned 0.979 (the book reports 89%); the old “0.888” anchor came from a different parameter set. The function now has a rho_b argument (Table 6.3 p_b), which defaults to rho1 for backward compatibility, and reproduces the book exactly: lambda = 14.0672, power = 0.893.
  • Legacy AUC and likelihood-ratio paths no longer return Inf. calculate_auc_single(), calculate_auc_superiority() and calculate_auc_comparison() used a mis-expanded Zhou Eq 6.4 variance (A(1-A) + (1/K)(Q1-A^2) + (Q2-A^2)) and divided by K = (1-P)/P, which is zero at the historical default prevalence = 1. They now use the printed Eq 6.4 variance function Q1/R + Q2 - A^2(1/R + 1); when prevalence is omitted the non-diseased:diseased ratio R falls back to 1 (a 1:1 case:control quota) and the deviation is reported in hints. calculate_likelihood_ratio_test() had the same P/(1-P) division and now falls back identically. This changes previously published numbers: auc_single(auc=0.8, d=0.05, prevalence=0.2) is 120 (was 366), aucSuperiority 26 (was 66), aucComparison 65 (was 122), likelihoodRatioTest 35 (was 120).
  • A’Hern (2001) citation corrected in calculate_ahern(), calculate_diagnostic_superiority_single() and the Chinese guide: the paper is Statistics in Medicine 20(6), 859-866 (doi:10.1002/sim.721), not British Journal of Cancer 85(2), 223-226.
  • Two more citation corrections verified against the source PDFs: Obuchowski (1994) is Investigative Radiology 29(2), 238-243 (not Medical Decision Making 14(2), 154-162); Simel et al. (1991) is Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 44(8), 763-770 (not 44(11), 1123-1130). Julious (2004) bioequivalence/crossover is Section 6.3 with Eq 6.1-6.9 (the non-central t power expression is Eq 6.8), not “Eq 13, p. 1941”.
  • alternative is now a real control argument of calculate(). It reproduces either Akoglu (2022) Table 2 Eq 2 (one-sided, the default that preserves existing numbers) or Hajian-Tilaki (2014) Eq 6.8 (two-sided). It is currently consumed by diagAccuracy + test + proportion only. The unimplemented sampling parameter has been removed from inst/reference/DESIGN_MATRIX.md, and the partial scope of dropout is now stated explicitly there and in ?calculate.

Output & Reporting Enhancements

  • Comprehensive Output Display: Default print() and summary() methods now consistently output:
    1. Plain-text mathematical formula (Formula (plain text))
    2. LaTeX mathematical formula (Formula (LaTeX))
    3. Step-by-step calculation process (Calculation process), documenting hypotheses, input parameters, critical values, intermediate components, and rounding
    4. Literature references (Reference)
  • Calculation reports now respect the selected AUC variance model and allocation, retain non-default power for diagnostic CI-width planning, and show the rounding used before cohort dropout inflation.
  • Calculation Steps In S3 Object: All sample_size_result objects now carry calculation and calculation_steps fields documenting the intermediate steps.

Numerical Enhancements & Cross-Package Alignments

  • diagLR: Corrected the log-LR variance to use sensitivity and false-positive probability for LR+, and false-negative probability and specificity for LR-. The published Se=0.90, Sp=0.50, upper LR-=0.40 example now requires 80 cases and 80 controls, rather than 9 per group. Both formula representations and the clinical guides use the corrected calculation.

  • singleCorrelation: Fixed implementation to strictly match Machin et al. (2018, Chapter 19, Equations 19.5-19.8). Now supports both precision (absolute CI half-width) and epsilon (relative precision). Produces exact agreement with presize::prec_cor (e.g., r=0.5, conf.width=0.10 -> 867; r=0.5, conf.width=0.20 -> 219).

  • bioequivalence: Upgraded 2x2 crossover TOST from crude normal approximation to exact noncentral t distribution (Phillips 1990; Julious 2004 Equation 13). Added support for theta0 (expected geometric mean ratio, default 1.0) and custom equivalence bounds (margin_low, margin_high). Results match PowerTOST::sampleN.TOST bit-for-bit (e.g., CV=0.25, theta0=1.0 -> N=24, 12/sequence; theta0=0.95 -> N=28, 14/sequence).

  • diagAccuracy (test): Added method = c("asymptotic", "exact"). Setting method = "exact" executes an exact binomial search per A’Hern (2001), returning critical successes critical_successes alongside sample size (e.g., prob=0.85, p0=0.70 gives n=49, critical cutoff r=40).

  • Methodological hints and parameter role clarifications added:

    • steppedWedge: Explicit warning regarding the absence of calendar-time fixed effects in Hussey & Hughes (2007) Equation 8 and potential power loss.
    • singleArmPhaseII: Documented that ties in minimax total N are broken by minimizing Type I error alpha.
    • caseControlMatched: Clarified that psi is the discordant pair proportion (pi10 + pi01), not the discordant odds ratio.
    • cohortRate: Clarified that required subjects = person-time / follow-up duration.
    • diagLR: Clarified that planning targets the approximate CI limit at the anticipated sensitivity and specificity, distinct from fixed-width CI estimation or assurance about every realized interval.

SampleSizeCalc 3.1.0

3.1 — new designs (mrmcPower, steppedWedge, kappa, Riley prediction models)

  • predictiveModel + task=“plan” + outcome=“binary”: Riley 2020 BMJ method for prediction model development sample size (original paper obtained and implemented). Criteria B1 (outcome proportion precision), B3 (shrinkage target via Cox-Snell R2), and B2 (van Smeden MAPE, P <= 30) with the entropy-based max R2cs helper. Anchors exact: B3 P=30/R2cs=0.05/S=0.9 -> 5249 (matches pmsampsize), B1 phi=0.5/delta=0.05 -> 385, B2 MAPE=0.05/ phi=0.3/P=10 -> 461 (Fig 2 worked example).
  • predictiveModel + task=“plan” + outcome=“rate”: Riley 2020 criterion T1 for time-to-event outcomes — person-years of follow-up needed for precise cumulative incidence under an exponential model (exact binomial-CI search; anchor: rate=0.10/yr, t=10y, delta=0.05 -> 2366 person-years, exactly the paper’s Figure 1 worked example).
  • mrmc_power(): power calculation for MRMC studies (paired-patient, paired-reader) using the Obuchowski-Rockette mixed model / non-central F framework (Zhou et al. 2011 Eq 6.32, Tables 6.3-6.4). Verified against the book’s mammography worked example (power ~= 0.89 at n=50, J=8, delta=0.10).
  • steppedWedge + task=“test”: Hussey-Hughes Eq 8 WLS Wald power for full stepped wedge designs (original paper obtained and Eq 8 implemented directly; the EPT figure-read anchor discrepancy is documented — Eq 8 gives power 0.959 at RR=0.64 and the 80% crossing at RR=0.73).
  • kappa + task=“estimate”/“test”: Cohen’s kappa sample size per Cantor (1996), using the Fleiss-Cohen-Everitt variance factor Q = po(1-po)/(1-pe)^2. Anchors exact: Q(0.5,0.5,0.7) = 0.510 and the two-questionnaire test N = 214. (Table 1/2 QMAX values require the full FCE lambda1 term; estimate mode is conditional on the planning kappa.)

Breaking / API

  • New unified three-axis entry point calculate(design, task, outcome, ...). Combinations are validated against a master table; illegal combinations error with the list of legal ones. See inst/reference/DESIGN_MATRIX.md. (sample_size_calculator() remains fully and silently compatible: all 17 legacy keywords now dispatch through the same shared code path, and golden-master tests assert identical results between both APIs.)
  • calculate() resolves arguments by exact name only. This fixes a latent partial-matching bug where design-specific arguments such as d could be silently swallowed into the design formal.

New features (Phase 5)

  • clusterRCT + task=“test” + outcome=“mean”/“proportion”: design-effect wrapper (DE = 1+(m-1)ICC) around the individually-randomised kernels, with cluster-level rounding (n_clusters per arm = ceil(nDE/m)) (Machin 2018 Ch.12; Donner & Klar 2000).
  • singleArmPhaseII: exact Simon two-stage designs (optimal = min E[N|p0], minimax = min N) via vectorised exact binomial search (Simon 1989), plus A’Hern single-stage (A’Hern 2001). Anchors verified against Machin 2018 Chapter 17: optimal (1/10, 5/29) and A’Hern 6/25, 12/35 reproduced exactly; the book’s minimax (2/15, 5/25) has exact power 0.7696 < 0.80 under the strict definition and is excluded (documented discrepancy).
  • rct + task=“noninferiority” + outcome=“proportion”: fills the legacy margin gap (nonInferiorityProportions).
  • twoOrdinal: ordered categorical two-group comparison via Whitehead’s formula N = 3(Za/2+Zb)2/((logOR)2(1-sum(p^3))) (Whitehead 1993; Machin 2018 Ch.4).
  • predictiveModel + task=“plan”: events-per-variable rule (EPV >= 10, Peduzzi 1996) with a pointer to Riley et al. (2019).
  • its + task=“test”: interrupted time series level-change power with an AR(1) effective-sample-size correction - marked EXPERIMENTAL in output hints (framework: Bernal et al. 2017; transparent approximation, not a validated source formula).
  • Deferred with documented reasons: kappa and steppedWedge (Machin Ch.20/Ch.13 formulas are OCR-garbled in the available PDF; require paper derivation before implementation).

New features (Phase 4)

  • Diagnostic non-inferiority/equivalence (margin designs):
    • diagAccuracyCompare + task=“noninferiority”/“equivalence”: two- proportion margin framework with one-sided alpha for NI and Z_{beta/2} for equivalence, plus prevalence screening conversion.
    • diagAUCCompare + task=“noninferiority”/“equivalence”: margin framework on the AUC difference with correlation r and all three variance functions (framework per Chow et al. 2017; application per Zhou 2011 Section 6.3).
  • diagAccuracyCompare + paired=TRUE via the three-axis API now uses the Connor kernel with psi = discordant-pair PROPORTION (the legacy keyword keeps the old sqrt-scale parameterization, locked by test).
  • crossover: 2x2 crossover with within-subject SD parameterization (n = 2(Za/2+Zb)^2 sigma_w^2 / delta^2; Senn 2002).
  • bioequivalence: 2x2 TOST on the log scale, 80-125% criterion (n = 2(Z_{1-a}+Z_{1-b})^2 log(1+CV2)/log(1.25)2; Schuirmann 1987; Julious 2004), with a replicate-design hint for CV > 30%.
  • diagAccuracy + dual=TRUE: dual-endpoint strategy computing sensitivity and specificity requirements each at dual_power (default 0.90 -> ~80% joint) and taking the max (Akoglu 2022 p.184).
  • Dispatcher gains a path flag (“legacy” vs “three-axis”) so upgrades can diverge cleanly from locked legacy behavior.

New features (Phase 3)

  • Observational study designs:
    • cohort + task=“test” + outcome=“proportion”: exposed vs unexposed cumulative incidence with 1:m allocation (ratio), optional dropout inflation, and RR parameter roles (Bhardwaj 2024 p.2559 anchor; exact-z value 294, paper’s rounded-z 293, ±1 documented).
    • cohort + outcome=“rate”: person-time incidence-rate comparison with unequal allocation (Machin 2018 Ch.6; IRR roles).
    • caseControlMatched: individually matched 1:1 case-control via the discordant-pairs formulation with the independence-within-pair approximation (Dupont 1988; Schlesselman 1982 p.174).
    • crosstab: cross-sectional prevalence comparison (PR/OR roles), sharing the two-proportion kernel.
  • paired + outcome=“proportion”: McNemar/Connor paired binary kernel with explicit discordant-pair proportion psi (Connor 1987; Akoglu 2022 Table 6A uncorrected anchor 155 at psi = delta = 0.05, 80% power).
  • rctSingleArm + task=“test”: single-arm vs fixed value for mean (Machin Ch.5) and proportion outcomes (Hajian-Tilaki Eq 6.8 anchor 153).
  • inflate_n() gains method = "additive" (n*(1+d), matching the arithmetic of the Bhardwaj worked examples) alongside the canonical “inflate” (n/(1-d)).
  • Result objects promote new metric fields: n_exposed, n_unexposed, person_time_exposed, person_time_unexposed, expected_events, n_pairs.

New features

  • Three estimation designs (task = “estimate”):
    • singleProportion: precision-based n = Z2*p(1-p)/d2 with absolute or relative precision and extreme-prevalence convention hints (Bhardwaj 2024 p.2558; anchor 323).
    • singleMean: n = (Z*sigma/d)^2 (Machin 2018 Ch.9).
    • singleCorrelation: Fisher-z precision n = ((1+r2)/(r*eps))2 + 3 (Machin 2018 Ch.19).
  • Diagnostic estimation upgrades (three-axis calls only; legacy keywords unchanged):
    • diagAccuracy + ci_method: “precision” (Zhou Eq 6.2) or “ci_width_power” (Zhou Eq 6.1, Flahault 2005; anchors 246/503).
    • diagAUC + var_method: “exponential” (Zhou Eq 6.4), “binormal” (Obuchowski 1994, Zhou Eq 6.5; CTC anchor 46/92), “conservative” (distribution-free, Zhou Eq 6.6; anchor 62/123); plus explicit case: control ratio parameter.
    • diagLR + lr_type/target_lr: log-LR CI method (Hajian-Tilaki 2014 Sections 6.4, Eqs 6.13/6.14) replacing the simplified Se/Sp-max formula for new-style calls.
  • New exported utility screen_required(n, prevalence, beta): total screening enrollment with an exact binomial probability guarantee of capturing n cases (Zhou 2011 Eq 6.3; anchor 451 at 350 cases, 80% prevalence, 90% guarantee).
  • Result objects gain hints (methodological warnings surfaced to the user) and n_required (single-sample estimation results).

New features (infrastructure)

  • New sample_size_result internals: new_sample_size_result(), validate_sample_size_result(), assert_sample_size_result() (internal three-piece constructor family) with canonical result fields (n_1, events, cases, subjects_to_screen, …) derived from legacy storage fields, preparing for new design modules in 3.0.
  • Internal numeric kernels z_alpha(), z_power(), inflate_n(), design_effect() shared by all future design modules (dropout inflation n/(1-d); cluster design effect 1+(m-1)*ICC).
  • as_sample_size_result() assembler so each design module can stay a plain calculation list.

Documentation

  • inst/reference/DESIGN_MATRIX.md: full design x task x outcome combination table with formulas, sources, and the 17 legacy-keyword mappings.
  • inst/reference/NUMERIC_ANCHORS.md: published worked examples used as numeric test anchors, including documented discrepancies (Bhardwaj 2024 dropout formula vs its own worked example).

Tests

  • Golden master suite: all 17 legacy keywords asserted identical between sample_size_calculator() and calculate() (228 assertions in the calculate suite alone).
